title: priority-eviction-bridge-for-controlled-regional-failover
author: Asha Narayanan
release_notes: Introduces a priority-based eviction bridge to coordinate graceful failovers across regions, adds preemptive KV-cache drain hooks for promoted replicas, and exposes a feature flag and conservative rollout plan.
description: Motivation: during cross-region outages we observed prolonged tail latency and cascading hot-spots when traffic was routed to promoted replicas that still had cold KV caches and large request queues. This PR introduces a Priority Eviction Bridge: a lightweight coordination layer that (1) allows a promoted replica to request preemptive KV-cache drain and high-priority slot allocation on target nodes, (2) enforces tokenized SLO credits when evicting lower-priority work, and (3) exposes a gated feature-flag with conservative defaults for rollout. Changes are scoped to the serving runtime and the scheduler shim so the feature can be toggled at runtime and rolled back without config migration. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests for eviction policy, [x] integration tests for drain path, [x] canary script for regional promotion, [x] observability dashboard and alert tweaks. Impact: improves failover latency and reduces error spikes by ensuring promoted replicas receive KV-cache prewarming and routing priority instead of competing with local transient bursts. Risk: scheduler behavior changes; default flag is off and rollout uses progressive canary to limit blast radius. See linked Linear items for rollout milestones and metrics to watch.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-03-01): Can you clarify how token accounting interacts with existing autoscaler slots? Concerned about double-counting across tenants.

Asha Narayanan (2026-03-01): Token pool is orthogonal to GPU slot accounting; added comments and diagram in token_accounting.go and the design doc to show separation. We only deduct priority tokens when preempting CPU work; autoscaler still governs GPU lease counts.
Maya Chen (2026-03-02): Suggest guarding the drain coordinator with a rate limiter to avoid thundering herd when multiple promoted replicas request prewarm simultaneously.
Asha Narayanan (2026-03-02): Added exponential backoff + jitter in drain_coordinator.go and a global per-region limiter. Also added tests to simulate concurrent promotions.
Diego Ramos (2026-03-03): Integration tests look good. One nit: use context timeouts for RPCs to avoid hanging drains during network partitions.
Asha Narayanan (2026-03-03): Addressed: added context timeouts and retry budget. CI flake fixed by increasing test harness timeout for simulated network jitter.
Maya Chen (2026-03-04): APPROVED after verifying dashboard metrics and canary script behavior in staging cluster.
testing: unit: eviction policy, token accounting, drain backoff logic
integration: two-region promotion scenario with simulated KV cold-start, validate latency/error curves
e2e: canary script 'promote_and_probe.sh' runs in staging and checks SLO burn rate < 2x baseline
load: sim_driver.py scenario runs to validate no regression in tail latency under mixed-priority workload
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag OFF in production, deploy code and metrics (canary disabled)
Phase 1: enable in 5% of traffic in staging-equivalent region, run canary script for 24h
Phase 2: progressive regional enablement (20% -> 50% -> 100%) over 3 days while monitoring eviction_bridge.topups and SLO burn
Rollback: toggle feature flag OFF and allow existing drains to complete (<= 5min)
notes: Backward compatibility: bridge is feature-gated and does not change default scheduler behavior when off
Observability: added SLO burn counters; on-call should watch eviction_bridge.evictions > 0 with concurrent regional promotions
Hotfix path: if unintended preemption occurs, ops can run opsctl revoke-priority <token-id> to immediately release reserved tokens
